---
title: "Edge security proposal"
description: "Review-only Cloudflare Pro rules that preserve browser, native, CLI and service traffic."
---

This is a draft proposal. Every proposed Cloudflare rule is disabled. No DNS,
rule, setting, Worker, deployment, or database change was applied. Finance and
Finance staging are excluded from every selector. A later change needs the
integration owner's admission and independent security review.

## Inventory and evidence

The [source inventory](/build/devops/edge-security-source) covers 1,824 app route
entries across 30 apps, 461 retained Web legacy implementations, 1,375 client
path literals, and manually traced native services. These are source counts,
not unique deployed endpoints. It records 563 unresolved auth classifications.

The [traffic snapshot](/build/devops/edge-security-traffic) joins 50 web/address
DNS names to current proxy status. Eight are proxied. Cloudflare returned 169
adaptive aggregate groups for the 24 hours ending 26 October 2026 at
13:58:25 GMT+7. Vercel initially returned retained first-page rows. A separate bounded follow-up
verified backwards time pagination, recovered Inventory rows and collected 2,267
matching-host rows. Twenty projects remain partial; central coverage reaches only
26 October 10:35 GMT+7. The two windows overlap and their counts are not additive.
Missing observations are unknown, not proof of no callers.

The rerunnable [census](https://github.com/tutur3u/platform/blob/main/infra/cloudflare/edge-security/inventory/source-census.jsonl)
includes source paths, methods, implementation forwarding, host candidates,
proxy status, applicable zone controls, auth signals, and caller classes.
Its first line defines scope and source revision. Each remaining line is a
route or client-path record. Generic auth signals require method-level review.
Custom domains such as `nova.ai.vn` and `rewise.me` need their own zone evidence.

## Supported Pro behavior

The zone read returned **Pro Website**. Existing authenticated GETs read the
settings and phase entrypoints successfully. The following capability claims
come from current first-party documentation, checked on 26 October 2026.
No rule was created to test write entitlement or expression acceptance.

| Capability | Evidence and consequence |
| --- | --- |
| Custom rules | Pro permits 20 rules and no `log` action or regex. The proposal uses neither. [Custom-rule availability](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/custom-rules/#availability). |
| Skip products and phases | `products: ["bic", "securityLevel"]` skips browser checks. `phases: ["http_request_sbfm"]` skips SBFM. Managed WAF and rate limiting stay active. BFM cannot be skipped. [Skip options](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/custom-rules/skip/options/). |
| Configuration rules | Pro permits 25. `set_config` belongs to `http_config_settings`; `bic` is boolean and `security_level` accepts `off`. These controls require proxied traffic. [Settings](https://developers.cloudflare.com/rules/configuration-rules/settings/), [availability](https://developers.cloudflare.com/rules/configuration-rules/#availability). |
| Rate limiting | Pro has 2 rules, IP counters, and counting periods through 60 seconds. Header/token counters require Advanced Rate Limiting. Existing leaked-password protection consumes one slot. [Rate limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/rate-limiting-rules/#availability). |
| Initial observation | `log` is Enterprise-only, including the rate-limit action. Pro uses disabled proposals, retained analytics, then a measured high threshold with `block`. A logged skip is an actual exemption, not a no-op log rule. [Actions](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ruleset-engine/rules-language/actions/). |
| Labyrinth | Its documented events inject links or record maze crawls; these events are not block/challenge actions. No documented per-path Labyrinth skip/config field was found. GET `/settings/ai_labyrinth` returned 400, not a valid control. Do not invent `ai_labyrinth` in Configuration Rules. [Labyrinth](https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/additional-configurations/ai-labyrinth/). |
| Bot protection | SBFM is included in Pro and supports scoped skips. Plain BFM does not. The current zone returns definite bots `allow`; a stronger zone-wide bot setting could affect Finance and is outside this proposal. [SBFM](https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/get-started/super-bot-fight-mode/). |

Live managed WAF and OWASP executions are enabled even though the legacy `waf`
setting is off. Existing Meet exceptions and the leaked-password rate rule
must be preserved. The proposal is an addition to reviewed entrypoints, never
a whole-ruleset replacement. A follow-up GET of the two managed definitions found CF version 418 with
866 block and 8 vendor log actions, and OWASP version 88 with 178 score actions
and one block action. Neither returned an enabled challenge action. Vendor-managed
log actions do not grant Pro custom/rate-rule log support. Refresh definitions
and zone overrides before rollout; keep narrow rule-ID false-positive exceptions.

## Traffic contracts

| Class | Proposed behavior | Required origin control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browser pages | Keep BIC and managed WAF. Full browser bot enforcement requires a separate Finance-safe admission for zone settings. | Turnstile on abuse-sensitive auth forms, checked server-side; ordinary session and tenant checks remain. |
| Authenticated APIs and bootstrap | Explicit app hosts and `/api/` paths skip BIC, Security Level and SBFM only. Missing/invalid credentials still reach origin rejection. | Validate bearer/app-session/API key or one-use bootstrap capability; scope permissions; per-token and per-IP quota. |
| Webhooks | Same challenge-free API transport. Published provider IP sets are reviewed as code in `webhook-origins.json`, initially observation-only. | Verify raw-body signature/shared secret before effects; replay/dedupe and bounded work. IP/ASN/UA never authenticates the event. |
| Realtime and service calls | Meet realtime enumerates HTTP and WebSocket paths outside `/api/`. Other service hosts remain unclassified until ownership is known. | Verify signed, expiring typed room/channel/collaboration ticket. Preserve query-token joins, Bearer HTTP calls, SSE, and upgrades. |
| Own page probes | Narrow GET/HEAD host/path plus dedicated secret header template. No UA or IP-only skip. | Public build metadata remains public; origin invalid-key canaries must still return 401. The edge header never replaces origin authorization. |
| Object delivery and external project hosts | R2/custom domains and unresolved aliases remain outside selectors. | Establish signed/public object contract, CORS, upload methods and source zone before extending transport exemptions. |

The machine selector is a transport classification. It does not assert that
every selected API is authenticated. It intentionally covers pre-login OTP,
CLI refresh, public delivery, cookie sessions, and invalid-token negative controls.
Exact Colab-style `/auth/login` and `/auth/callback` redirects, discovery metadata,
and `/.well-known/` are classified separately from browser auth forms. A new
`/auth/register` page retains browser controls.
No rule skips managed WAF, rate limiting, remaining custom rules, or application
authentication. A managed-rule false positive requires a narrow rule/path exception.

Existing auth code already verifies Turnstile in
`apps/web/src/lib/auth/otp.ts:329` and `packages/turnstile/src/server.ts:170`.
Preserve the native proof flow and hostname/action validation. The
[Turnstile contract](https://developers.cloudflare.com/turnstile/get-started/server-side-validation/)
requires server-side validation and single-use tokens. Do not place interstitial
challenges in front of the mobile/CLI bootstrap API or require desktop cookies.

## Files and local verification

`infra/cloudflare/edge-security/policy.json` owns host/path selectors.
`rulesets/custom.json`, `configuration.json`, and `rate-limit.json` are generated
review fragments. They contain five disabled rules and no deploy command.
`webhook-origins.json` contains published Square and Polar environment CIDRs,
required signature checks, and observation prerequisites. It is not an API payload.

```sh
node scripts/edge-security-rules.mjs --write
node scripts/edge-security-rules.mjs
node --test scripts/edge-security-rules.test.mjs
```

The validator checks exact compiled output, Finance exclusions, disabled state,
Pro counter fields, expression size, probe scope, and narrow skips. Tests reject
enabling rules, UA-only identity, broad skips, published probe secrets, Finance
selectors, token-based Pro counters, and unsupported configuration drift.
This validates the local proposal contract; it is not Cloudflare expression or
plan-entitlement validation. No provider API is called by these commands.

The high-threshold candidate is **6,000 API requests per 60 seconds per IP/colo**
on Meet only, with a 10-second block. This is an uncalibrated initial ceiling,
not a measured safe threshold. Shared NAT, internal fanout, polling, caching and
provider retries must be measured before admission. It excludes conventional
webhook/cron prefixes; nested hooks need explicit owner classification before
expanding the host set. Keep the existing leaked-password rule and its ID intact.

Per-token limits cannot be represented by this Pro edge rule. Enforce them after
authentication in existing portable service boundaries, using stable token IDs
or hashes rather than raw credentials. Any new Cloudflare limiter must have
bounded calls/retries, idempotent progress, terminal states and a tested durable
stop fence before rollout. This PR creates no runtime, queue, timer or datastore,
and adds no Supabase/Vercel dependency.

## Rollout and rollback proposal

All steps below are future operator work. Finance custody and the independent
review are prerequisites. No step is authorized by merging these documents.

| Order | Admission and acceptance | Rollback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Resolve source gaps | Establish live deployment and credentials for External, Playground and legacy Supermemory. Review AI adapter signatures and unresolved auth contracts. Refresh host/phase snapshots. | Make no edge change; preserve known ownership and record unresolved gaps. |
| 2. Observe and prepare | Capture all available retained traffic, label sampling/pagination, and measure API burst/NAT/provider distributions. Reconcile remaining Pro slots. Privately provision a rotated probe header and update only admitted probes. | Remove the new probe header at callers and revoke its value; preserve origin canaries and auth. |
| 3. Canary transport exemptions | Add only reviewed, disabled fragments to existing entrypoints; then separately admit one non-Finance canary host. Verify origin 401/403, valid APIs, native OTP/refresh, cookies, CLI, signed webhooks, upgrades/SSE, and browser pages. | Disable added rules by their returned IDs. Preserve existing managed exceptions and rate rule; do not replace a whole entrypoint. |
| 4. Browser enforcement | Confirm machine/control/callback/object paths are complete. Keep BIC on browser pages. Admit stronger SBFM settings only after Finance releases its hold, with all affected hosts covered. Labyrinth remains unchanged without proven per-path controls. | Restore only the recorded prior bot/config values, under zone owner custody. Keep exact before/after receipts. |
| 5. High-threshold flood limit | Preserve leaked-password protection. Admit the remaining one Pro rate-rule slot on a single host only after burst evidence. Verify no HTML challenges and retry behavior with bounded fixtures. | Disable only `edge_machine_flood`; retain per-token app limits and existing rate protection. |
| 6. Provider IP filters | Compare verified Square/Polar deliveries against freshly published production/sandbox sets. Enforce only with signature/replay checks, an owner and a list-refresh procedure. Unknown providers stay signature/shared-secret authenticated. | Revert the new IP restriction while retaining signature checks and dedupe. Never add broad cloud-ASN/IP authentication bypasses. |
| 7. Extend hosts | Admit one owner at a time, including DNS-only origin acceptance before a separate proxy cutover. Custom domains need their own zone evidence. | Restore the recorded host/rule state for that admitted host; DNS changes remain a separately scoped release. |

Any unexpected challenge, valid signature rejection, origin 401 regression,
stalled socket/stream, or rising accepted-caller failures stops expansion.
The owner disables the new rule first and reconciles provider state before retry.
No blind replay, automatic global rollout, new monitoring controller, or
production/database change is part of this proposal.
